item.title: Townsend hails Scotland's defence in Australia 'arm wrestle'
item.description: Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend hailed his team's defensive efforts after they edged past Australia in a Nations Championship "arm wrestle" at Murrayfield. Off the back of being dismantled by New Zealand last weekend, in which they failed to score a second half point, the spotlight fell on Scotland's leaky defence. But on a chilly and damp Edinburgh day where physicality was king, they delivered a much-needed win and showed they are capable of winning ugly. Even so, Townsend's side didn't make it easy. Max Jorgensen's late converted try gave the Wallabies hope, and with the clock in the red, the visitors broke from their own half. Murrayfield held its breath, but Darcy Graham hauled Australia full-back Tom Wright into touch with a superb tackle. "When we saw the rain half an hour before kick-off, you still hope you'll be able to move the ball," Townsend said. "You could tell defences were coming off the line a bit quicker, knowing they could pressure the ball carrier. "Both teams had to adjust and I thought we did that well. Defensively, that's one of the best performances I've seen in the last couple of years. Set after set we were putting them under pressure. "We were on that edge of physicality but disciplined, hitting hard in the tackle, putting pressure on, listening to the referee, getting back onside. That makes it hard for the opposition to get into our 22m, which was a learning from last week. "It was just constant effort. Today, we showed we can play another game, too." Final whistle a blessing as Scotland edge dull Test against Australia Nations Championship: Scotland hang on for scrappy win over Australia - as it happened Leading 12-5 at half-time, there was one eye on whether Scotland could clinch a bonus-point victory that would have both boosted their points difference and helped their chances of climbing the northern hemisphere table with Japan to come on Saturday. However, it soon became apparent that would not be forthcoming in a match that will not live long in the memory. "It was about winning at all costs today," former Scotland prop Peter Wright said. "We hoped we might get something quite end-to-end, 50 points to 48, loads of tries, but to come out on the right end of a war of attrition like that, it's a good feeling. "When you're Scottish, winning's always good. We very rarely win in style at any sport. We just want to get victories under our belt. "It was a bad game last week so getting some momentum going into the Japan game next week was really important. "I thought the pack was outstanding." item.title: To Carmelo Anthony, there is an obvious reason for Jayson Tatum - Jaylen Brown rift
item.description: While some fans and analysts of the Boston Celtics may be surprised by the supposed ire between former costars on the wing Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown as they wonder what might be the root cause of it, to Hall of Fame forward Carmelo Anthony, the answer is a simple, structural one. For the former Denver Nuggets and New York Knicks icon, there is no need to psychoanalyze the two longtime teammates. "From my understanding, it's organizational structure, right?" said Anthony on a recent episode of his "7 PM in Brooklyn" podcast. "It's business at the end of the day." "And you put two guys who built something together, drafted their All-Stars together, finals MVP, championship, all of these things that they accomplished together for the organization," he added, "for the business to come in and play that part and draw a wedge in that and then leave it to the two players to figure it out." "I think it put those two guys in uncomfortable situations that both of these guys are trying to do the same thing," said the former Knicks legend. "We won together. Okay. Now I'm an alpha, you're an alpha. Just we are not going to be alphas together anymore. And the business of it put a lot of friction in the middle of that." item.title: Celtic Track Ligue 1 Ball-Winner For January: Is He The Engels Answer?
item.description: Celtic Track Ligue 1 Ball-Winner For January: Is He The Engels Answer? CeltsAreHere reports on X that Simon Ebonog is far more than another name on a long Celtic shortlist. The Le Havre midfielder is under serious consideration at Parkhead, and Celtic are monitoring him ahead of a possible January bid, although no formal move has been made yet. The timing makes sense. Martin O’Neill has said Celtic must go back into the market for an Arne Engels-type midfielder in January after the summer failed to produce a like-for-like replacement, and Callum McGregor turns 33 next month. Celtic lead the Premiership by four points after Liam Scales beat Kilmarnock, yet a 2-2 draw with Dundee United and a 0-2 defeat at Falkirk came within four days around the turn of the month. What Ebonog offers Ebonog is a 22-year-old, right-footed defensive midfielder from Yaoundé who has started all 10 of his Ligue 1 appearances for Le Havre this season, 877 minutes in total. His strength is winning the ball. He has made 19 tackles and 16 interceptions, and he has won 55.4 per cent of his duels. He also keeps things simple in possession, completing 88.9 per cent of his passes, and one yellow card suggests he wins the ball cleanly. The limits are just as clear. He has no goals or assists in those 10 starts, his FotMob rating sits at a modest 6.99, and a hamstring problem cost him time last December. Le Havre extended his contract until 2029, so they hold the leverage, and FotMob values him at €6.4m, around £5.5m, his highest ever. Should Celtic make Ebonog their January priority? GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – NOVEMBER 08: Celtic manager Martin O’Neill arrives prior to the William Hill Premiership 2026/27 match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Only if he arrives as the second midfielder through the door. Engels gave Celtic goals and forward passing from a deeper role, and Ebonog offers neither. He is a screener who protects the back line and recycles possession, and that has real value because McGregor cannot play at this level forever and Celtic need a succession plan. The harder issue is what O’Neill’s side actually lacks. Scottish opponents sit deep at Celtic Park, so the gap is a midfielder who breaks that block with a pass or a late run, not another who wins the ball back. A fee near £5.5m would suit a 22-year-old with that defensive output, but his contract means Le Havre will ask for more. Celtic should identify the creator first. If Ebonog comes alone, O’Neill will have solved McGregor’s succession and left Engels’ goals unreplaced.

item.title: Harry Kane talks building a Champions League dynasty with Bayern Munich
item.description: Photo by Sven Hoppe/picture alliance via Getty Images Harry Kane has achieved numerous honors with Bayern Munich since his arrival, but one piece of silverware has eluded his trophy cabinet: the Champions League. The Bavarians famously won the trophy three times from 1974 to 1976 (when it was still called the European Cup); now, the club continues its search for a seventh UCL win. “I’ve always said that my goal is to win the Champions League with Bayern,” Kane said (via Sport Bild’s Christian Falk as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “Winning it with this team would be a very special feeling. I would be lying if I said that I didn’t want to win the Champions League with Bayern at least once. We’ve already won many trophies together, and every time it’s an incredible feeling. So, I’m sure that being crowned champions of Europe would feel equally incredible.” Bayern last won the Champions League in 2020 and came dangerously close a few times since then, most notably the narrow eliminations in 2024 and earlier this year (as part of last season’s UCL cycle). item.title: Could Ketel Marte Trade Be Orioles' Next Pete Alonso-Sized Splash?
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles are far from a contender in the American League -- or even in the AL East, for that matter. But that hasn't stopped them from looking to add star power. The latest big name who could be coming to the Inner Harbor is Ketel Marte, who reportedly has been the subject of conversations between the Orioles and Arizona Diamondbacks. The mercurial second baseman's stock is low following a subpar season that saw him disappear on the team and be placed on the restricted list. But the O's have prospects to burn and some pressure to compete after last winter's monster investment in first baseman Pete Alonso. In reporting the talks on Saturday, MLB.com's Jake Rill stipulated that no deal was imminent. Still, it's hard to see what Baltimore president of baseball operations Mike Elias' plan is. The O's inked Alonso to a five-year, $155 million deal last offseason, then traded franchise fulcrum Adley Rutschman to the Boston Red Sox at this year's MLB trade deadline. Replacing struggling second baseman Jackson Holliday with Marte would be a sensible win-now move, but it clashes with the future-oriented decision to deal away Rutschman to create room for Samual Basallo at catcher. Marte holds a no-trade clause, so in addition to finding a trade package that would work for both teams, the player would also need to be convinced. With Marte's relationship with the Diamondbacks apparently deteriorating, however, it's believed he would welcome a change of scenery. item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Kyle McCord #14 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the Indianapolis Colts during an NFL football game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins faced the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, with starting quarterback Kyle McCord in his NFL debut after an injury to Malik Willis. A game featuring two teams in contention for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, it felt like that at times. Neither team executed a complete game, but in the end, the Colts held on to squeak out the win. The Dolphins fell to 1-8 with the loss to the Colts. They had chances to win this game, but they lost after three kicks failed to put points on the board. The game was put on the shoulders of a young quarterback, and he responded. The offense moved the ball well enough to win the game. The defense shut down the Colts’ offense, especially in the second half. The Dolphins should be walking out of Indianapolis with a win. In the end, the special teams failed Miami. In the long run, this game could prove important to the Dolphins as they look toward the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami falling to 1-8 keeps them in contention for the first-overall pick and pushes the Colts further away from claiming it. Even better, the Colts’ pick is owned by the New York Jets after a trade last year. Not allowing an AFC East division rival to jump them in the draft order could be a way to find a silver lining on an ugly black cloud of a day.
